agm-f2a.headline: Human Written
windows: Agmatine, the "voltage regulator", acts like a brake on NMDA/glutamate signaling, which is why we do use it in this protocol. But we'll keep it as an optional add-on, since it can interact with a lot more medications than the protocol's safer nutrients would (magnesium, phosphatidylcholine, etc.). People may think it's pretty safe, since it's a common health supplement, but we have to treat it with caution since it acts powerfully on imidazoline/alpha-2 adrenergic receptors, nitric-oxide pathways, and opioid reward/tolerance.

rule-f2a.headline: Human Written
windows: My rule for now is to seek "Boring Love", meaning parallel play (like reading next to someone) and touch that feels safe to you. A new romance or high-stakes drama gives you the rush of "Exciting Love", which spikes Phasic Dopamine and puts the armor right back up. So this may not be a good time to jump into a new romance or drama, though there's no need to leave the partner you have.

prec-f2a.headline: Human Written
windows: Do not use agmatine concurrently with opioids and/or kratom (will reduce tolerance), clonidine and/or guanfacine, blood pressure lowering medications (including nitrates and PDE-5 inhibitors), or other complex psychoactive stacks (anything that works on the brain, beyond what this protocol pairs it with) without having a physician competent to consider the likelihoods of problematic interactions. It's not recommended for use in pregnancy or breast-feeding. Use it with extreme caution in those with a prior psychotic episode, lower end blood pressure, or kidney or liver issues.

iso-f2a.headline: Human Written
windows: This neural de-armoring protocol demands starving your brain of "Phasic" Dopamine, which works in the brain to produce learning and excitement when chasing novelty. The easiest way for most folks to take a break from that is to hole up alone. But don't isolate completely (the isolation trap), because that actually spikes cortisol, the chronic stress hormone. And cortisol sensitizes your brain to glutamate, thus locking the old neural armor in place that we're trying to gently remove. Calm company, like nature walk buddies, goes the other way, anchoring you via oxytocin, the bonding hormone. Good friends are ultimately more vital than any brain repair protocol.
